 Chapter 1O9 authorizes the creation of the new Council. The legislature provides that the Governor of Alaska is to form the Alaska Safety Council by the appointment of such members as he may desire from among the Departments of Territorial and Federal government and the gen. eral public who are particularly concerned with safety programs and accident prevention.

attain people of Johnstown
and those affiliated with "St.
Rochus" CFU Lodge 5 were
greatly saddened recently, at
the news that the Grim Reap
er had removed from our
midst sister Anna Tomasic,
one of our oldest and most re-
spected members.


Following a lengthy illness,
sister Tomasic passed away
on February 10Th, 1855, at
the Lee Homeopathic Hospi-
tai. She was sixty-eight years
Of age.


Sister Tomasic was born in
1886 in Karlovac, in Croatia.
In 1902 she was united in
marriage to the late Joseph
Tomasic, who passed away in
1888, here in Johnstown.


= Our beloved late sister join
ed the ranks of the Croatian
Fraternal Union in 1921 and
since that time had devoted
endless hours of work in
Lodge activities. She was al
so an ardent worker as an af-
filiate Of the st. Rochus Cro-
atian Church and the Altar
Society until such time as her
illness forced her to retire.


Through these associations
sister Tomasic acquired a
host Of friends in Johnstown
and vicinity, and the memory
of her humanitarian deeds
will long remain with us.


She is survived by sons Jo-
seph, our erstwhile Lodge 5
president and current Sick
Benefit Secretary, Frank who
is a resident of New York,
and daughters Mrs. John Kr-
eel, Versailles, Pa, Mrs. Eliz-
abeth Schovinsky, Johnstown
Pa, Mrs. Mary Burgess, New
York City, Mrs. Mildred Gall,
Johnstown, Pa, and Mrs. Ca
therine Salinger of Detroit,
Mich.


A brother, John Mihelic, re-
siding in Europe, ten grand
children and one great
grandchild, Joseph Krcel of
Versailles, also survive.


Hundreds of friends and
